subject.title: chore(deps): bump the production-minor-and-patch group across 1 directory with 22 updates

question: Should maintainers accept this grouped production dependency bump as one merge, or require the higher-blast-radius dependency updates to be split first?
rationale: The patch appears mechanically correct and validated, but it intentionally changes broad production dependency surfaces where rollback, bisection, and release-risk tolerance are maintainer calls.

options.title: Accept grouped bump
options.body: Merge this as normal weekly dependency maintenance, relying on the green CI/preview while accepting the grouped compatibility risk.

options.title: Split riskier packages
options.body: Ask for narrower PRs around Convex, TanStack, Sharp, and CLI/schema parser updates so any regression is easier to isolate.

options.title: Hold for targeted smoke proof
options.body: Pause until a maintainer runs focused smoke checks for the most important app, CLI, email, Markdown, and image-generation paths.

recommendation.title: Accept grouped bump
recommendation.body: Merge this as normal weekly dependency maintenance, relying on the green CI/preview while accepting the grouped compatibility risk.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest package/dependency-config history signal and was also mentioned on the PR timeline.
